summary: Avebe is a Dutch farmers' cooperative, founded in 1919, that processes starch potatoes grown by its members into potato starch and potato protein ingredients for food, animal nutrition and industrial uses. It is based in Veendam, with production sites in the Netherlands, Germany and Sweden, and has more than 2,000 members.
ownership: Farmers' cooperative with more than 2,000 members
products: Potato starch derivatives, including starch ethers
Ingredients for plant-based dairy and meat, bakery, soups, sauces and snacks
Ingredients for petfood, farm animal feed and aquafeed
Starch products for paper, building and construction, and adhesives
markets: Customers around the world, with sales offices in the UK, USA, China, Singapore, Taiwan and Japan
Starch ethers stocked worldwide through a network of distributors
facts: More than 2,000 members and a team of 1,300 professionals
Averis varieties make up at least 80% of the seed potatoes Avebe growers use
First Solanic protein factory opened in Gasselternijveen in 2007
Innovation Center opened in Groningen in 2018
2030 target: cut ecological footprint by 30% compared to 2022/2023

contact.address: Prins Hendrikplein 20, 9641 GK Veendam, the Netherlands

limitations: The pages read do not publish tonnes of potatoes processed, plant capacities, what each plant makes, turnover or starch potato hectares.
The site says Avebe holds several certificates but does not name them, and no variety names are given.
